East Maryland took incredible care of Skye throughout all of our visits this past year. The vets and vet techs were always kind, friendly, and they always provided us with the best experience possible.

Our only negative experience was with the Paw Plan. We were encouraged to sign up because of the benefits it offered, including necessary vaccinations, stool samples, and spay surgery, etc. During the process, we were specifically told that Skye’s spay would be covered, which was the main reason we felt the Paw Plan was worth it.

After her surgery, we were surprised by several additional costs that had not been clearly communicated to us and we ultimately received a much higher bill than expected. While we were very happy with the care Skye received, we felt the Paw Plan was not explained enough.

If you’re considering signing up, I would strongly recommend asking plenty of questions and getting a clear understanding of exactly what is and isn’t covered. Based on our experience, we would have chosen not to sign up if we could go back.

To the Management and Medical Staff at East Maryland Animal Hospital,
Attn: Dr. Melana B. Martens, D.V.M.
I am writing to formally express my deep dissatisfaction and outrage regarding the repeated mishandling of my cat’s medical care at your facility. This letter is not written lightly. It follows multiple visits over a period of time in which I explicitly requested that his anal glands be examined—each and every time.

Despite these repeated and direct requests, your team either dismissed the concern outright or assured me that it had been checked when, clearly, it had not. Instead, I was subjected to a series of costly and unnecessary tests, vague assessments, and ultimately, a complete failure to address the core issue that has now led to an emergency room visit.

This neglect was not a simple oversight. It was systemic, apathetic, and costly—not just financially, but in terms of my cat’s health and comfort. The signs were clear. My communication was clear. Your inaction is inexcusable.

You charged us for services you either failed to perform or performed negligently. You assured us that anal glands were not the problem when they were the problem all along. The distress my cat has experienced because of your clinic’s failure to follow through on a simple, routine check is indefensible. Had your staff performed the examination I requested—and was billed for—this painful situation could have been avoided entirely.

I will be forwarding the emergency room invoice, as it is the direct result of your clinic’s negligence. I also plan to share my experience with my community so others can make informed decisions before trusting your clinic with their pets’ care.

If your clinic is unable or unwilling to handle the basics of preventative veterinary care, or if your staff cannot follow through on standard procedures—even when requested—you should not be accepting new clients, much less charging for services you did not provide.

You owe my cat an apology. And you owe us one, too.

My first visit here wasn’t terrible, but it also wasn’t great. While the technicians I encountered were kind and professional, my experiences with the veterinarians have been disappointing. During our last visit, the vet continued to rip my cat out of her carrier, despite my suggestion—twice—that we remove the top for a gentler approach. Which is what the tech did prior to her entering the room, and what has been done every other time.
As someone with 20 years of healthcare experience, I found it concerning when the vet seemed frustrated —made a comment about having to look through her EXTENSIVE history — about reviewing my cat’s medical history after I inquired about whether a three-year vaccine was even due, after they kept bringing it up. Organizationally, such information should be readily accessible.

Additionally, after following their request to consult a dental specialist, I explained the specialist told me that while her teeth are bad they aren’t horrible so she didn’t see an immediate need. Considering my cat’s very serious condition involves her mouth I decided to hold off on dental cleaning as the risks of immediate dental work outweighed the benefits for my cat’s condition. The response I received was “That’s not what the report says.”

Thankful that others have had good experiences but I personally will not be back.
